name: The Generative Horizon: Applied Hermeneutics, Linguistic Attractors, and the Limits of Model Self-Report
headline: The Generative Horizon: Applied Hermeneutics, Linguistic Attractors, and the Limits of Model Self-Report
description: This preprint introduces the generative horizon and recursive interpretive conditioning as an applied-hermeneutic framework for analyzing how prompts, context, memory, self-reports, decoded features, and retained outputs shape later interpretation and action in large language model systems. It connects model self-report, reasoning-trace faithfulness, mechanistic interpretability, linguistic attractors, provenance, supersession, and epistemic engineering while preserving a strict boundary between measured representations and claims about inner observers or phenomenal awareness.
